extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of GAP (computational algebra system); programmers referencing GAP's data representations and string API
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual chapter describing available vector/matrix representations and the full string/character API in GAP, including predicates, representations, printing rules, escape sequences, string operations, conversions, and calendar/time utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGF2VectorRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsGF2VectorRep describes a vector object with entries in the finite field with 2 elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies IsCopyable (thus vector objects can be mutable). References IsVectorObj (26.2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Is8BitVectorRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in Is8BitVectorRep describes a vector object with entries in a finite field with q elements, for 3 ≤ q ≤ 256.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The base domain is not necessarily the smallest field containing all entries. Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPlistVectorRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsPlistVectorRep describes a vector object that can occur as a row in a row list matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 26.12; implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsZmodnZVectorRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsZmodnZVectorRep describes a vector object with entries in a residue class ring Z/nZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ring is the base domain of obj. Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGF2MatrixRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsGF2MatrixRep describes a matrix object with entries in the finite field with 2 elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaves like the list of its rows (IsRowListMatrix); base domain is field with 2 elements. Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Is8BitMatrixRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in Is8BitMatrixRep describes a matrix object that behaves like a list of its rows with base domain a finite field of size 3..256.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The base domain must contain all matrix entries but need not be minimal. Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPlistMatrixRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsPlistMatrixRep describes a matrix object that behaves similar to a list of its rows (IsRowListMatrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsZmodnZMatrixRep
rubrics_metrics.description: An object obj in IsZmodnZMatrixRep describes a matrix object with entries in a residue class ring Z/nZ and which behaves like a list of its rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ring is the base domain of obj. Implies IsCopyable (mutable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsChar / IsCharCollection
rubrics_metrics.description: IsChar(obj) identifies a GAP object representing an arbitrary character from the OS character set; IsCharCollection is related category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character literals entered in single quotes. Examples show IsChar('a') true.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsString
rubrics_metrics.description: IsString(obj) identifies strings as dense lists of characters; strings are homogeneous and can be entered as lists of characters or double-quoted literals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP outputs strings with double quotes; double-quote input may give a compact internal representation. Strings must be dense and contain only characters. Examples show equality of list form and quoted form; IsString([]) and IsString("") behavior discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings As Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings in GAP are special cases of lists, so list operations apply (indexing, membership, length, concatenation, substrings, assignment to mutable strings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning non-character values or making the list non-dense will make it no longer a string. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing Strings (ViewObj/PrintObj/Print)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings displayed by View/ViewObj/PrintObj are shown with enclosing doublequotes; Print/PrintTo/AppendTo interpret a string by sending its characters directly to the output stream (subject to stream and special-character behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empty string vs empty list ambiguity: ConvertToStringRep distinguishes. PrintObj output can be read back; Print prints actual characters (including newlines). Examples show differences and escaping behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Character Escape Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined escape sequences beginning with backslash include \n (newline), \" (doublequote), \' (singlequote), \\ (backslash), \b (backspace), \r (carriage return), \c (flush), \XYZ (three octal digits), \0xYZ (hex digits); other sequences ignore backslash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing behavior, how to input characters not directly typable, and advice that only Print/PrintTo/AppendTo send characters directly to output. Triple-quoted strings ignore these escape rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple Quoted Strings
rubrics_metrics.description: Triple quoted strings begin and end with three doublequotes and ignore the escaping rules; they include newlines until three doublequotes are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internally represented identically to other strings; still follow GAP's line editing rules. Example demonstrates literal inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsStringRep
rubrics_metrics.description: IsStringRep is an internal representation of dense lists of characters; strings can be converted to this representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calling IsString does not change representation; ConvertToStringRep and CopyToStringRep operate with this representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConvertToStringRep
rubrics_metrics.description: ConvertToStringRep(obj) changes a dense list-of-characters into internal IsStringRep representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for converting the empty list [] to an internal string representation; signals an error if obj is not a string.

rubrics_metrics.name: CopyToStringRep
rubrics_metrics.description: CopyToStringRep(obj) copies a dense list-of-characters to a new object with IsStringRep representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals an error if obj is not a string.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsEmptyString
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEmptyString(str) returns true if str is the empty string in the internal IsStringRep representation, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes empty list [] vs empty string ""; recommended for formatted printing which sometimes requires the distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: EmptyString
rubrics_metrics.description: EmptyString(len) returns an empty string in internal representation with allocated memory for len characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to preallocate and fill a string of known length. Paired with ShrinkAllocationString to return unused memory to GAP's memory manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShrinkAllocationString
rubrics_metrics.description: ShrinkAllocationString(str) gives back to GAP's memory manager the physical memory allocated for an internal representation string beyond its current character count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to save memory in specific situations; analogous to EmptyPlist/ShrinkAllocationPlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharsFamily
rubrics_metrics.description: Each character lies in the family CharsFamily; each nonempty string lies in the collections family of this family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note subtle differences between printing the empty list [] and empty string "".

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDigitChar
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDigitChar(c) checks whether character c is a digit (occurs in "0123456789").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple predicate for digit membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLowerAlphaChar
rubrics_metrics.description: IsLowerAlphaChar(c) checks whether character c is a lowercase alphabet letter (in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate for lowercase letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUpperAlphaChar
rubrics_metrics.description: IsUpperAlphaChar(c) checks whether character c is an uppercase alphabet letter (in "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate for uppercase letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAlphaChar
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAlphaChar(c) checks whether character c is either a lowercase or uppercase alphabet letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined alpha test.

rubrics_metrics.name: String equality and inequality ( = and <> )
rubrics_metrics.description: The equality operator = returns true if two strings are equal; inequality <> returns true if they are not equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons are case sensitive; examples show newline presence matters. Strings and list-of-chars comparisons behave as expected (e.g., [ 'a','b' ] = "ab" is true).

rubrics_metrics.name: String ordering ( < )
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordering of strings is lexicographic according to the underlying system-dependent character set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate ASCII semantics where capitals precede lowercase and prefixes are smaller. Strings can be compared with certain non-string GAP objects; see 4.13 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayString
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayString(obj) returns a string usable to display obj in a nice, formatted way (human-readable); each method should include a trailing newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No method for DisplayString may delegate to Display, ViewObj or PrintObj to avoid circular delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEFAULTDISPLAYSTRING
rubrics_metrics.description: DEFAULTDISPLAYSTRING is the default value for DisplayString.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global variable controlling default display formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: ViewString
rubrics_metrics.description: ViewString(obj) returns the string that ViewObj would display for obj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No method for ViewString may delegate to Display, ViewObj, DisplayString or PrintObj (avoid circular delegations).

rubrics_metrics.name: DEFAULTVIEWSTRING
rubrics_metrics.description: DEFAULTVIEWSTRING is the default value for ViewString.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global default for view-string behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintString
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintString(obj[, length]) returns a string representing obj intended to approximate the sequence seen when printing obj using PrintObj; optional length pads result to minimal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If length given, absolute value is minimal length; positive fills on left, negative on right. Two-argument call returns a new mutable string. PrintString may insert control chars \< (ASCII 1) and \> (ASCII 2) to allow line breaks; use StripLineBreakCharacters to remove them.

rubrics_metrics.name: String (attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: String(obj[, length]) returns a string representation of obj approximating PrintObj output; behaves like PrintString but must not insert control characters \< and \>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-argument call returns new mutable string; padding rules same as PrintString.

rubrics_metrics.name: StripLineBreakCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: StripLineBreakCharacters(st) removes control characters \< (ASCII 1) and \> (ASCII 2) used for line breaking, returning a new string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to sanitize PrintString/PrintObj output when these control characters are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: HexStringInt
rubrics_metrics.description: HexStringInt(int) returns a string representing integer int in hexadecimal (A-F used for 10-15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse is IntHexString; useful for storing/reading large integers efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringPP
rubrics_metrics.description: StringPP(int) returns a string representing the prime factor decomposition of integer int.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: StringPP(40320) -> "2^7*3^2*5*7". See PrintFactorsInt for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: WordAlp
rubrics_metrics.description: WordAlp(alpha,nr) returns the nr-th word over alphabet list alpha in word-length then lexicographic order; the empty word is WordAlp(alpha,0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show enumeration of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowercaseString
rubrics_metrics.description: LowercaseString(string) returns a lowercase version of string by mapping uppercase alphabet characters to lowercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided; behavior limited to alphabet characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowercaseChar
rubrics_metrics.description: LowercaseChar(character) returns the lowercase version of the given character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-character analog of LowercaseString.

rubrics_metrics.name: UppercaseString
rubrics_metrics.description: UppercaseString(string) returns an uppercase version of string by mapping lowercase alphabet characters to uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: UppercaseChar
rubrics_metrics.description: UppercaseChar(character) returns the uppercase version of the given character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-character analog of UppercaseString.

rubrics_metrics.name: SplitString
rubrics_metrics.description: SplitString(string, seps[, wspace]) splits string into substrings at occurrences of characters in seps or wspace; wspace characters are treated as whitespace sequences and ignored at ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both seps and wspace can be single characters. Characters in result do not contain separators or whitespace. A separator at end acts as terminator and does not produce trailing empty string. See Chomp as alternative for newline trimming.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReplacedString
rubrics_metrics.description: ReplacedString(string, old, new) replaces occurrences of substring old in string by new, starting from the left and always replacing the first occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid infinite recursion, already-replaced characters are not subject to renewed replacement. Examples show replacement order effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalizeWhitespace
rubrics_metrics.description: NormalizeWhitespace(string) changes string in place by treating space, \n, \r, \t as whitespace: trims leading/trailing whitespace and replaces sequences between characters by a single space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NormalizedWhitespace returns a non-destructive copy instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalizedWhitespace
rubrics_metrics.description: NormalizedWhitespace(str) returns a copy of str with NormalizeWhitespace applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-destructive version of NormalizeWhitespace.

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: RemoveCharacters(string, chars) efficiently removes all characters in chars from string (both args must be strings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows removing whitespace characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: JoinStringsWithSeparator
rubrics_metrics.description: JoinStringsWithSeparator(list[, sep]) joins a list of strings, interpolating sep (default ",") between adjacent strings; sep should be a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show joining with space or multi-line separators; useful for producing readable concatenations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chomp
rubrics_metrics.description: Chomp(str) removes a trailing newline character (or carriage-return line-feed couplet) from str if present and returns the result; otherwise returns str unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe to use on non-strings or values that might be fail as it returns them unchanged. For splitting into lines, use SplitString.

rubrics_metrics.name: StartsWith / EndsWith
rubrics_metrics.description: StartsWith(string, prefix) and EndsWith(string, suffix) determine whether a string starts or ends with another string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boolean predicates for prefix/suffix testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringFormatted / PrintFormatted / PrintToFormatted
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting functions that accept a format string with replacement fields { } and data...; StringFormatted returns formatted string, PrintFormatted prints it, PrintToFormatted appends to stream or file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement fields can have id and format separated by '!': {id!format}. id can be integer, a string (record field access), or omitted (then positional). Formats: s (String), v (ViewString), d (DisplayString); default is s. Doubling braces outputs literal braces. Examples demonstrate positional, named, and formatting usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumbersString
rubrics_metrics.description: NumbersString(s, m[, table]) encodes string s to a list of integers each ≤ m using scheme A=11, B=12,... converting lowercase to uppercase; an optional table list may be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for toy examples like text encryption; example shows encoding into large integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringNumbers
rubrics_metrics.description: StringNumbers(l, m[, table]) decodes a list l of integers (encoded by NumbersString) back into a message string using scheme A=11, B=12,...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates decoding to uppercase message.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringOfMemoryAmount
rubrics_metrics.description: StringOfMemoryAmount(numbytes) returns a human-readable string representing numbytes using binary prefixes (powers of 1024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for printing memory amounts in tests/benchmarks; example: 123456789 -> "117MB".

rubrics_metrics.name: IntChar
rubrics_metrics.description: IntChar(char) returns an integer in range [0..255] corresponding to char.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-dependent mapping (ASCII/extended).

rubrics_metrics.name: CharInt
rubrics_metrics.description: CharInt(int) returns a character corresponding to integer int in range [0..255].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CharInt(65) -> 'A'.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIntChar
rubrics_metrics.description: SIntChar(char) returns a signed integer in range [-128..127] corresponding to char.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed mapping useful for certain conversions; relation to IntChar shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharSInt
rubrics_metrics.description: CharSInt(int) returns a character corresponding to signed integer int in [-128..127].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed/unsigned functions agree on [0..127].

rubrics_metrics.name: Int (for strings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Int(str) returns an integer as represented by string str; optional leading '-' allowed; empty string accepted for backwards compatibility returning 0; other inputs return fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show valid and invalid inputs; returns fail on non-integer strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rat (for strings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rat(str) returns a rational number represented by string str; optional leading '-' allowed; accepts integers or two sequences of decimal digits separated by '/' or '.' (decimal dot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other inputs return fail. Examples show conversion of "123/45" and "-123.45".

rubrics_metrics.name: IntHexString
rubrics_metrics.description: IntHexString(str) parses a possibly signed hexadecimal string into an integer; letters a-f/A-F used for 10-15; other inputs cause an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for efficient large-integer I/O; example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinal(n) returns the ordinal string of integer n (e.g., 2 -> "2nd", 21 -> "21st").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handles negative numbers as well; examples show typical ordinal suffix rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EvalString
rubrics_metrics.description: EvalString(expr) passes the string expr through an input text stream so GAP interprets it and returns the result; intended for single expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple commands use InputTextString and ReadAsFunction. Inside a function EvalString cannot see local variables; workaround: assign locals to globals before EvalString. Examples and a pattern provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: CrcString
rubrics_metrics.description: CrcString(str) computes a cyclic redundancy check (CRC) integer from string str.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related functions: CrcFile and HexSHA256. Example shows numeric CRC result.

rubrics_metrics.name: HexSHA256 (for string or stream)
rubrics_metrics.description: HexSHA256(string) or HexSHA256(stream) returns the SHA-256 checksum of the bytes as a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For streams, reads from current position to EOF. Example demonstrates checksum of "abcd".

rubrics_metrics.name: Pluralize
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluralize([count,] string[, plural]) returns a guessed or supplied plural form of an English singular noun string; optional count prepends "\>n\< " quoting control characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plural provided it's used; if count omitted returns plural form; if count given and ≠1 prepends count, if 1 prepends quoted 1. StripLineBreakCharacters can remove the quoting control characters. Examples show common irregulars and numeric prepending.

rubrics_metrics.name: DaysInYear
rubrics_metrics.description: DaysInYear(year) returns the number of days in the specified year (Gregorian calendar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Gregorian rules; example shows 1998 -> 365.

rubrics_metrics.name: DaysInMonth
rubrics_metrics.description: DaysInMonth(month, year) returns number of days in given month of year, or fail if month invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided; uses Gregorian calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMYDay
rubrics_metrics.description: DMYDay(day) converts a number of days since 1-Jan-1970 to a list [day, month, year] in Gregorian calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts from epoch; examples illustrate conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: DayDMY
rubrics_metrics.description: DayDMY(dmy) returns number of days from 01-Jan-1970 to the day given by dmy = [day, month, year]; returns fail on invalid ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes limitations for historical dates (pre-Gregorian adoption) where results may be meaningless.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeekDay
rubrics_metrics.description: WeekDay(date) returns the weekday of a date given as days-since-1970 or [day, month, year].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns string like "Wed"; examples included.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringDate
rubrics_metrics.description: StringDate(date) converts date to a readable string; date can be days-since-1970 or [day, month, year].

rubrics_metrics.name: HMSMSec
rubrics_metrics.description: HMSMSec(msec) converts milliseconds msec into [hour, min, sec, milli].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example with Factorial(10) demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: SecHMSM
rubrics_metrics.description: SecHMSM(hmsm) is the inverse of HMSMSec, converting [hour, min, sec, milli] to milliseconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to switch between representations; example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringTime
rubrics_metrics.description: StringTime(time) converts time (number of milliseconds or [hour, min, sec, milli]) to a readable string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting for human-readable time; examples implied by other functions.
